First balance the exchange: a change in piece count is not a change in value. Consider which pieces were exchanged and who gets the initiative afterward. One extra piece in the count alone does not prove a gain.
King safety comes first. In check, examine legal evasions. Outside check, still ask whether the opponent can build a concrete follow-up threat.

Think of the squares around the king as doors. More attacked squares enlarge the warning zone. This counts attack coverage, not legal escape squares; inspect checks, blocks and captures before judging safety.
The center is a transport hub. Occupying it can support coordination, but the occupying piece can become a target. Is it defended, and can the position be maintained under attack?
A piece can influence central squares from a distance. More attack coverage can affect development, but is not necessarily an immediately legal capture. Pins and king safety still matter.
Development means useful cooperation, not merely leaving home. This count only describes placement. Ask whether the new square helps, obstructs a teammate, or costs time through repeated moves.
Rooks and cannons need routes. More legal destinations suggest activity, not a proven attack. Check cannon screens, targets and possible blocking replies before deciding the maneuver is worthwhile.

An occupied horse leg restricts movement. Consider clearing the blocker or taking another route, but check whether the blocking piece is also guarding the general. Activity is not worth dismantling a necessary defense.
Connecting may merge groups, but captures can also reduce the group count. Verify the cause on the board, then count the liberties after connecting. Connected does not automatically mean alive.
One liberty is an alarm, not a death sentence. Look for extension, connection or countercapture. Ko can change the legal options. Do not chase an enemy group while overlooking your own weaknesses.

Count liberties for the whole group without counting shared liberties twice. An extra liberty can buy room to act. If a connected group remains short of liberties, compare connecting with extending or countercapturing.

Legal moves and ko have been checked for this immediate capture opportunity. It does not mean the opponent must take it. Before playing elsewhere, decide which stones you can afford to give up and what you gain in return.
